summary:
Cosall is an interactive web application that helps users learn about, plan, and set timelines for lunar missions. Whether an educator is teaching students, an amateur is curious about lunar missions, or and expert looking towards getting a serious, honest first pass for their missions, Cosall satisfies their needs.

Cosall's backend acquires the open source NASA data and presents it according to the user's inputs. This lets the user to know the appropriate timeline, landing site, launch date for their hypothetical mission. The tools Cosall provides are built around one core principle : the horizon visibility (of the Sun and the Earth).

Planning missions to the moon, especially to its south pole is a challenging task and the tools necessary for it are usually unavailable to the general public or are complex. Cosall removes the barriers and enables access to everyone. It is simple and sufficient.

This is the core motive for our team — 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝗆𝗈𝗌 𝖿𝗈𝗋 𝗮𝗹𝗹.
details:
Introduction

Cosall is an interactive web application which lets the user to visualize the Sun-Earth-Moon motion and get instant feedback on DTE communication potential and Sun visibility (Orbit View), choose an appropriate landing site and compare various sites (Site Planner), get a suggestion on launch date based on various factors taken into consideration (Launch Planner).

Objectives

  1. Create an interactive web application focused on ease of use and user experience.
  2. Ground every result in real data.
  3. Make space mission planners accessible.

Cosall aims to be a part of the movement towards bringing cosmos to everyone.

Techstack

Backend (Python, deployed on Render as cosall-api)

  • FastAPI for the web API, served by uvicorn
  • SpiceyPy (NASA NAIF SPICE toolkit) for Sun, Earth, and Moon ephemerides and lunar orientation
  • NumPy and SciPy for the geometry, the horizon calculation, and interpolation on the terrain grid
  • rasterio and pyproj for reading the LOLA terrain model and converting coordinates
  • Matplotlib for the offline analysis scripts (the figures in docs/figures)

Frontend (JavaScript, deployed on Render as the static service cosall)

  • React 19 for the interface
  • Vite 8 for the build and dev server
  • Three.js for the 3D Earth-Moon-Sun orbit scene
  • Plain SVG for the horizon chart, timelines, and ribbons, with no charting library

Deployment and data

  • Render runs both services from one render.yaml Blueprint
  • download_data.py fetches the SPICE kernels and the LOLA DEM at build time, since they aren’t stored in Git
  • Python 3.13 and Node 22 are pinned by .python-version and .node-version

Navigating through the Software

Hero Page

This is the first section of the application featuring a brief introduction, a cool art (SI-assisted) and navigation buttons.

To spice things up, clicking on Cosall in the hero page will take you to a story-style walkthrough (named Silent Landing ) of our project's necessity and functionalities. Click on it for an immersive experience.

Orbit View

Orbit View lets you visualize the Sun-Earth-Moon orbit (based on real ephemeris data) and get an instant result on whether DTE communication and Solar potential is possible or not.

The results are based on the site chosen by the user in "Site Planner". Enter date, rate of animation and play or pause as needed.

Additionally, orbit view has two perspectives. You can watch the story unfold as a third person or in moon's perspective. Our personal favorite is the site's view which gives a breathtaking visual as well as a visual confirmation of Earth and Sun's visibility over the horizon based on terrain data from LOLA.

Clicking on the terrain map will show the terrain map visualization generated by backend/terrain_map.py based on LOLA data.

Architecture of Orbit View

The shown Flow Chart is made with the help of Super-Intelligence (Claude).

Site Planner

This section is used to select and compare landing sites either from a selected popular landing sites or your custom coordinates (Note that Cosall does not provide terrain data for sites to the north of 60S and hence assumed flat). At the moment, Cosall does not suggest landing sites based on chosen timeline, we hope to include that feature in the near future.

Select a landing site and get a plethora of results to get a clear picture. If that sounds slow, you can compare up to 3 sites at the same time with the help of "Compare Sites" feature.

Architecture of Site Planner

Flow chart made with SI-assistance

Launch Planner

This section will help you to get suggestions on when to launch from the Earth so that when you land on moon, you can say hi to Earth and as well as get the appropriate vitamin D.

Select the site, scan starting date, launch site, transit time and evaluation period. 10 launch dates over the course of next 5 years will be suggested ranked based on a hypothetical (educated guess) weighted formula. The results will be based on the evaluation period (for example Sun is visible for 76.1% means it is visible for that percent over the evaluation period after landing) . Click on a suggested launch date to get more information.

Architecture of Launch Planner

Flow chart made with SI-Assistance.

About Us Page

This page will give clear picture on who we are, why we made this project, the data used, project's limitations. Future plans are listed in the project's demonstration while the limitations are listed in the website's about page.

Benefits

Cosall gives different audiences a practical way to work with lunar south-pole geometry.

  • Educators and students can see how the Sun and Earth move across a real terrain horizon, which makes orbital mechanics and lunar illumination concrete instead of abstract.
  • Curious members of the public can explore the Earth-Moon-Sun system in 3D, check the Moon’s phase and distance for any date from 1960 to 2050, and see why the south pole is both scientifically interesting and difficult to reach.
  • Early-stage mission planners can compare candidate sites and landing dates on sunlight, Earth visibility, and dark or blackout stretches, and shortlist a few options before commissioning detailed analysis.
  • Anyone gets results without specialist software. The tool runs in a browser, uses open NASA data, and states its assumptions and limits next to each result.

Novelty

Cosall combines several things that are usually found only in separate, specialist tools:

  • Terrain-aware visibility for the south pole. Each site’s horizon is computed from NASA’s LOLA 80 m and 240 m elevation model, so hills and crater rims affect the results.
  • A single view of sunlight and Earth contact. Sun and Earth visibility are computed together and shown as one timeline, so users see where the two overlap.
  • Launch-window scanning. Cosall scans years of candidate landing dates, scores each one, and works back to a launch date for a chosen Earth launch site and transfer time.
  • Transparent, checked results. The About page compares the outputs with published Apollo 11 values and with analytic test cases, and it lists the model’s limits.
  • Open and free. It is built entirely on public NASA data and open-source software, with the aim of making lunar planning available to anyone.

Cosall is a culmination of our passion to contribute and passion to one day, experience the view Cosall provides with our own eyes. Eagerly waiting for the next giant leap for mankind. Thank you for judging our project.

Application : https://cosall.onrender.com
